text: {"features":[{"name":"Mechanical polish","description":"Measures how free the letter is from spelling, grammar, and proofreading mistakes that affect professionalism.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent errors, including prominent mistakes in names, greetings, or technical terms, repeatedly distract and undermine the impression of care."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Multiple noticeable spelling or grammar errors appear throughout the letter, but the overall meaning is still recoverable."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"A handful of scattered errors or awkward phrasings are present, yet the letter still reads as reasonably professional."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Only one or two minor, easy-to-ignore slips appear, with no visible mistakes in prominent role or company details."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter is exceptionally polished, with virtually no noticeable mechanical errors and a fully professional presentation."}]},{"name":"Narrative distinctiveness","description":"Measures whether the letter presents a memorable personal angle or through-line rather than a generic statement of interest.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter reads as generic and interchangeable, with no clear hook, point of view, or unifying thread."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows a faint attempt at personal framing, but most of it remains formulaic or list-like."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter has a recognizable hook or angle that makes the application somewhat memorable."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter sustains a clear narrative or perspective that ties the applicant's experiences to the role."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter delivers a distinctive, coherent story of fit that remains memorable while still sounding professional and role-focused."}]},{"name":"Evidence specificity","description":"Measures how concretely the letter supports its claims with specific projects, technologies, responsibilities, and outcomes.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter relies mostly on broad assertions of skill or fit with little concrete supporting detail."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter includes a few specifics, but many important claims remain abstract, ungrounded, or outcome-free."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter uses several concrete examples of work, tools, or problems to support key claims."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly grounds claims in specific technical examples and operational contexts that make the fit believable."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter consistently backs claims with precise, role-relevant examples and clear results, making the case highly credible."}]},{"name":"Role motivation","description":"Measures how specifically and convincingly the letter explains why the applicant wants this exact role on this team.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The stated interest is generic and could apply to many software engineering roles."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions security, Google, or the team in broad positive terms without much specific reasoning."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives clear role-specific reasons tied to security engineering or automation work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The motivation is strong and well matched, clearly connecting the posted work to the applicant's background and goals."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes the role feel like a natural next step by tightly linking the team's mission, responsibilities, and the applicant's trajectory."}]},{"name":"Platform leverage orientation","description":"Measures how strongly the letter demonstrates interest in foundational systems whose improvements benefit many teams.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows little evidence of interest in shared infrastructure or organization-wide leverage."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter expresses a general desire for impact or scale without linking it to platform-style work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly states attraction to foundational, central, or infrastructure-level engineering."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter strongly frames prior work or future goals around multiplier effects and improvements inherited by many teams."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter consistently articulates a platform mindset, emphasizing central systems, compounding leverage, and organization-wide benefit."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement orientation","description":"Measures how clearly the letter values making secure behavior easier for other engineers through tooling and defaults.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter says little about serving developers or reducing friction for users of the tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter uses generic collaboration language without showing a clear developer-enablement mindset."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly values helping engineers do the secure thing more easily or reducing manual toil."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter emphasizes building tools and defaults that fit real developer behavior rather than relying on process or documentation alone."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents developer enablement as a core philosophy, backed by examples of making the secure path the easiest path at scale."}]},{"name":"Security engineering mindset","description":"Measures how thoughtfully the letter frames security as an engineering discipline with proactive, design-oriented practices.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter treats security mainly as a label or area of interest, with little deeper perspective."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows general enthusiasm for security but limited explanation of how security should operate in engineering practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter articulates at least one sound principle such as secure defaults, proactive assistance, or attacker-minded review."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows a thoughtful philosophy of security as design work embedded in systems and workflows rather than paperwork."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter conveys a mature, nuanced view of security as high-standard engineering that combines proactive design, adversarial thinking, and operational practicality."}]},{"name":"Reliability mindset","description":"Measures how strongly the letter conveys concern for maintainability, failure modes, operational care, and what downstream teams inherit.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives little indication of thinking about reliability, maintenance, or long-term ownership."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions dependable systems or maintenance only in passing and without substance."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or describes testing and operations as important experience."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows a strong maintainer mindset through examples involving inherited services, failure cases, quiet stability, or operational care."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes reliability thinking central to the application, with vivid evidence of designing for failure, maintainability, and downstream ownership."}]},{"name":"Security partnership orientation","description":"Measures how well the letter shows readiness to work closely with security specialists and the teams the tooling serves.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no real indication of working closely with security experts or tool users."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter sounds generally collaborative but does not connect collaboration to this role's stakeholders."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter explicitly values working alongside security engineers or close to the teams being supported."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter explains how proximity to security specialists or users improves the quality and adoption of the tooling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter frames close partnership with security experts and served developer teams as central to how the applicant builds effective systems."}]},{"name":"Academic alignment","description":"Measures how strongly the applicant's academic background exceeds or matches the role's preferred technical preparation.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows only the minimum academic baseline, such as a bachelor's degree in a relevant field, with no further technical preparation highlighted."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows a bachelor's degree plus additional technical formation beyond the minimum, such as advanced certifications, research exposure, or ambitious systems work, but no advanced degree."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows a master's degree in computer science or a closely related technical field."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows a doctoral degree in computer science or a closely related technical field."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows a doctoral-level background that is explicitly tied to the advanced rigor useful for security, AI, or algorithm-heavy work."}]},{"name":"Professional track record","description":"Measures the depth of the applicant's production software experience in testing, maintaining, operating, and launching systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter barely exceeds the baseline, with a short tenure and limited scope such as only a couple of launched services."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows credible production experience, but either years of practice or delivery breadth remains modest."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows solid mid-level production experience across testing, maintenance, and launches with repeated ownership."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong production depth through longer tenure or a higher number of launched services, indicating repeated end-to-end delivery."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows especially strong production depth by combining sustained tenure with substantial launch, maintenance, and operational responsibility across multiple services."}]},{"name":"Scale-of-impact evidence","description":"Measures how much the letter demonstrates experience building systems or tools that operate on high-volume paths or serve many teams.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no clear evidence of work at significant technical or organizational scale."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter suggests interest in scale but provides little evidence of broad usage or high-throughput systems."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives at least one credible indication of systems with meaningful load, organizational reach, or shared use."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong evidence of high-throughput, hot-path, cross-team, or organization-wide systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly demonstrates experience with large-scale or broadly used internal platforms whose impact extends well beyond a single team."}]},{"name":"Go backend depth","description":"Measures how convincingly the letter establishes Go as a primary language for relevant backend or infrastructure work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter mentions Go only briefly or without any sense of primary responsibility."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter identifies Go as an important language but gives little detail on what was built with it."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly presents Go as a primary production language in backend or service work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter links Go experience to building or operating backend, infrastructure, or systems software with concrete examples."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes Go depth a central part of the case, showing substantial responsibility for backend systems that are especially relevant to security or automation."}]},{"name":"Python depth","description":"Measures how convincingly the letter establishes production-grade Python experience relevant to tooling, automation, or AI.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not mention Python or implies only negligible exposure."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions Python as a secondary language without clear production ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly uses Python in production for tooling, internal services, automation, or analysis."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes substantial Python responsibility with concrete examples such as services, test harnesses, automation layers, or internal systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows especially strong, role-matched Python depth through ownership of significant automation, internal services, or agent-based systems built in Python."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"Measures how strongly the letter shows practical command of data structures and algorithms.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not mention algorithmic work or gives no evidence of this capability."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter makes a broad claim of algorithmic strength without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter supports algorithmic ability with one specific example of an optimization or redesign."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter gives a strong example in which a data structure or algorithm meaningfully improves performance, tractability, or system behavior."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes algorithmic fluency especially convincing through technically specific examples that materially transform a hard problem or critical path."}]},{"name":"Security assessment depth","description":"Measures how much hands-on experience the letter shows in evaluating systems for security weaknesses and following issues through.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no clear evidence of performing security assessments."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions reviews or security work vaguely, without method or scope."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly states experience with security assessments, threat modeling, or vulnerability-focused code review."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes structured assessment work with concrete methods such as attack-surface mapping, documented findings, or validation of fixes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents security assessment as a strong recurring practice, with nuanced perspective and clear ownership of remediation or design-level analysis."}]},{"name":"Applied AI depth","description":"Measures how strongly the letter shows hands-on experience building and hardening production AI features.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no AI experience or only expresses interest in learning it."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions AI in general terms without clear evidence of production use."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows direct production exposure, such as shipping model-backed or LLM-enabled features."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter couples AI delivery with evidence of evaluations, guardrails, reliability work, or awareness of failure modes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows especially strong AI fit by combining production delivery, reliability discipline, and relevance to the role's security automation context."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems architecture","description":"Measures how much the letter demonstrates experience designing autonomous or semi-autonomous agent systems with clear controls.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not mention agents or multi-step autonomous systems."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter refers vaguely to agents or automation without explaining architecture."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly describes building agentic pipelines or systems involving agents and supporting services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter adds concrete control concepts such as permissions, contracts, task decomposition, boundaries, or auditing."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows sophisticated, role-matched agentic design in which autonomous agents are deliberately constrained, observed, and supported by robust backend systems."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability-response automation","description":"Measures how directly the letter shows experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, or related response workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of work on vulnerability-response workflows."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows general interest in security automation but no direct vulnerability-handling experience."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter clearly describes building automation for vulnerability intake, classification, deduplication, routing, or triage."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows that this automation materially reduced manual work or turned an ad hoc queue into a repeatable process."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents vulnerability automation as a high-leverage strength, showing strategically designed workflows that meaningfully scale security capacity."}]},{"name":"Offensive security practice","description":"Measures how much the letter shows attacker-oriented practice through certifications, competitions, or explicit offensive learning.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no concrete evidence of offensive-security practice."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows only light or indirect offensive-security signal."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows some real offensive-security engagement, such as recurring CTF participation or a foundational certification."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong attacker-side practice through advanced certification, serious competition results, or sustained offensive work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows especially compelling offensive-security credibility by combining advanced hands-on credentials or top competition performance with an attacker-minded framing of the work."}]},{"name":"Self-directed engineering initiative","description":"Measures how strongly the letter shows technical ownership beyond assigned job duties through open-source work or substantial personal builds.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no meaningful evidence of technical initiative beyond the day job."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions a small side project or occasional outside contribution with limited scope or continuity."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows consistent outside initiative through a maintained project, regular open-source contributions, or a self-directed technical build."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter demonstrates substantial ownership or ambition outside work, such as maintaining an active open-source project or building a nontrivial distributed system."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows outstanding self-directed initiative through sustained, technically ambitious work that also signals craftsmanship, community responsibility, or deep systems curiosity."}]}]}
